title: Dell Precision 7680 Common Issues & Fixes
content:
### Frequent symptoms
- Coil whine or fan surge under light loads when Dell Optimizer power profiles are disabled.
- Thermal throttling during CAD/render workloads caused by dust-packed fin stacks.
- USB4/TB4 docks intermittently dropping displays after sleep.

### Troubleshooting workflow
1. Update BIOS to 1.16.0+ and Intel ME firmware from Dell Command Update.
2. Run SupportAssist hardware scans; escalate if thermals exceed 95°C sustained.
3. For docking instability, install the latest Intel graphics and Thunderbolt controller drivers, then reset the dock’s firmware by unplugging power for 30 seconds.
4. Re-seat SO-DIMMs if SupportAssist memory diagnostics fail, then rerun ePSA.

### Dell ePSA / SupportAssist error codes
- 2000-0123 – Memory integrity failure. Steps: test each DIMM in slot A only; replace the failing module.
- 2000-0141 – No hard drive detected. Steps: verify NVMe seating, toggle RAID/ACHI in BIOS, and replace SSD if absent in BIOS.
- 2000-0151 – CPU fan failure. Steps: clear dust, inspect fan cable, replace heatsink assembly if RPM remains 0.
- 2000-0511 – GPU fan failure. Steps: same as CPU fan; document temps for Dell escalation.

### Escalation notes
- Capture thermal logs from SupportAssist and HWinfo64.
- Provide dock model, cable length, and external monitor specs for graphics-related tickets.
- Include BIOS export (F12 setup) and service tag in the escalation email.

title: Dell Precision 7670 – Known Field Issues
content:
### Frequent symptoms
- Battery swelling or chassis lift near the clickpad after 18+ months of heavy charge cycles.
- Intermittent keyboard backlight outages tied to BIOS 1.9.x.
- NVMe throttling when the bottom cover vents are obstructed by desk mats.

### Troubleshooting workflow
1. Inspect battery physically; if swollen, disconnect power immediately and replace the pack.
2. Update BIOS to 1.14.x or newer and reset EC via 30-second power drain.
3. Reflash keyboard firmware through Dell Peripheral Manager when backlight zones fail.
4. For storage throttling, reseat NVMe with new thermal pad and run ePSA drive tests.

### Common error codes
- 2000-0161 – RTC power failure. Steps: replace coin-cell battery and reset BIOS defaults.
- 2000-0155 – Thermal sensor failure. Steps: verify fan harness, update BIOS, replace heatsink assembly if code persists.
- 2000-0142 – Drive self-test cannot be completed. Steps: clone critical data, secure erase, replace SSD if SMART fails.

### Escalation checklist
- Attach thermal screenshots and battery photos.
- Provide SupportAssist log bundle (.zip) and AC adapter wattage.
- Confirm part availability before authorizing onsite service.

title: Dell Precision 7580 / 7570 Support Playbook
content:
### Frequent symptoms
- POST hang at Dell logo when discrete GPU is enabled.
- Fan cycling loudly at idle because of Dell Optimizer performance profiles.
- USB 3.1 ports dropping power to scanners/printers during remote sessions.

### Troubleshooting workflow
1. Update BIOS and GPU firmware; if POST hang persists, toggle switchable graphics off, boot, then re-enable after driver refresh.
2. Run Dell Optimizer, select Quiet mode, and update Intel Dynamic Platform & Thermal Framework drivers.
3. Disable USB selective suspend in Windows power plan and update chipset drivers.
4. Reset SupportAssist OS Recovery partition when Windows repair loops are reported.

### Error codes to track
- 2000-0131 – CPU cache failure. Steps: reseat CPU (for serviceable units) or escalate for motherboard replacement.
- 2000-0415 – USB controller failure. Steps: test bare-bones boot, reseat daughterboard, replace system board if persistent.
- 2000-0712 – Alert! TPM self-test failure. Steps: clear TPM in BIOS, update firmware, replace system board if the error remains.

### Escalation checklist
- Include GPU model, driver versions, and dock/peripheral list.
- Document BIOS revision and whether legacy/UEFI boot is enabled.
- Attach SupportAssist hardware test screenshots.

title: All Dell PCs – High-Frequency Error Codes & First Response
content:
### Top SupportAssist / ePSA codes
- 2000-0111 – CPU fan failure. Steps: reseat fan cable, check fan spin in BIOS diagnostics, replace fan.
- 2000-0123 – Memory integrity failure. Steps: test modules individually, swap slots, replace module or motherboard.
- 2000-0141 – No hard drive detected. Steps: reseat storage, update BIOS/SATA mode, replace drive if absent in BIOS.
- 2000-0142 – Drive self-test cannot be completed. Steps: back up data, run OEM drive firmware update, replace drive if SMART fails.
- 2000-0151 – CPU temperature sensor failure. Steps: clean heatsink, refresh thermal paste, replace thermal assembly.
- 2000-0152 – System board failure. Steps: disconnect non-essential devices, perform BIOS recovery, escalate for board swap.
- 2000-0162 – Battery temperature error. Steps: inspect battery, update BIOS, replace battery if swollen or failing.
- 2000-0165 – AC adapter wattage cannot be determined. Steps: test with known-good adapter, inspect DC-in jack, update BIOS.
- 2000-0170 – Hard drive error detected. Steps: reseat or replace drive after cloning data.
- 2000-0511 – GPU fan failure. Steps: inspect GPU fan cable, clean vents, replace GPU heatsink/fan module.

### Universal intake questions
1. Confirm service tag, OS build, BIOS version, and dock/peripherals.
2. Ask about recent changes (Windows updates, driver installs, hardware additions).
3. Check SupportAssist history for recent failed updates or repairs.
4. Gather event viewer critical logs and minidumps for blue-screen cases.

### First-response checklist
- Run F12 diagnostics (ePSA) and capture the reference number.
- Update BIOS, chipset, storage, and graphics through Dell Command Update.
- Verify Windows power/battery reports with `powercfg /batteryreport`.
- Document any third-party encryption or security software before OS repair.
- For thermal complaints, photograph vent obstructions and log fan RPM/temps.

### Escalation package
- ePSA reference, SupportAssist log bundle, system inventory export, photos/videos.
- Steps already attempted, OS rebuild status, and warranty coverage confirmation.
- Customer impact assessment and requested next action (onsite, depot, parts).

title: 3Shape TRIOS 3/4/5/6 Scanner Troubleshooting Knowledge Base
content:
### Hardware & Connectivity Differences
- **TRIOS 3** uses USB-A 3.0 with an external power pod; firmware below 1.4.9 is prone to USB selective suspend dropouts on Windows 10 21H1. Disable USB power saving on hubs and update to the latest Unite-certified firmware before replacing cables.
- **TRIOS 4** adds built-in battery and Wi-Fi for pod-less operation. Frequent disconnects usually trace back to depleted smart batteries (<15%) or outdated Wi-Fi dongle firmware. Cycle the batteries monthly and keep pod firmware at 1.6.x to stabilize sleep recovery.
- **TRIOS 5** introduces a pen grip with LED scanner status ring and wireless charging puck. Most wake failures are caused by clogged contact pads—clean with 70% IPA and reseat the puck. Replace the magnetic cable if LED stays amber after 30 minutes on charge.
- **TRIOS 6** ships with USB-C hardwiring and new field-replaceable tips with thermal sensors. USB-C cables longer than 2 m cause enumeration failures; stick to the 1.8 m shielded cable bundled by 3Shape.

### Calibration & Optics
- **Shared drift symptoms**: washed-out surfaces, double contours, or occlusion holes. Always verify the tip glass is seated and cool (below 40 °C). Run Unite → Settings → Scanners → Calibrate; expect green checks within 3–5 minutes.
- **TRIOS 3/4** rely on the black/white calibration tile. If the tile is warped or matte finish is worn, scans skew 50–100 µm; replace the tile yearly.
- **TRIOS 5/6** use the Sphere Calibration unit. Error 1060 typically indicates the sphere QR code is unreadable—clean the window and re-register the accessory under Scanner Tools.
- If the scanner rejects calibration with error 3112/3113, confirm that the Unite PC regional format uses a dot decimal separator; commas interfere with calibration data parsing in firmware <1.5.2.

### Thermal & Fan Alerts
- **TRIOS 3** internal fans clog easily in dusty labs. Unite logs will show warning 20102 (over-temperature). Blow compressed air through the vent slots and check fan RPM via TRIOS Diagnostic Tool. Persisting warnings require fan module swap.
- **TRIOS 4** triggers Battery Overheat warnings if scanning continuously on Wi-Fi dock; switch to pod power for long cases and update firmware to leverage the revised thermal curve introduced in 2022 Q4.
- **TRIOS 5/6** log Code 47 when tip thermistor exceeds 48 °C. Cooling the tip under running water (never submerge handle) for 30 seconds resolves most cases. Document ambient room temps >28 °C for escalation.

### Image Quality & Color Issues
- **Grainy or color-shifted scans** often come from smudged mirrors. Use lint-free swabs with 70% IPA; never use acetone on TRIOS 5/6 sapphire windows.
- Firmware 1.7.x introduced HDR color capture; ensure Unite 23.2 or later is installed. For older PCs, disable HDR in Unite → Settings if GPU is Intel UHD 620 or lower to prevent stuttering.
- For **TRIOS 3** units showing banding, verify the USB pod firmware matches the scanner firmware. Mixed firmware levels lead to exposure desync (Support FAQ ID 1157).

### Wireless & Battery Checks (TRIOS 4/5/6)
- Use 3Shape Battery Tool to read cycle counts. Replace packs once capacity falls below 80% to avoid sudden shutdowns mid-scan.
- Wi-Fi dropouts while using Move+ carts commonly stem from DFS channel interference. Configure the access point to fixed channel 36/40 and keep the scanner within 5 m line-of-sight.
- LED sequence reference: solid green = ready, pulsing blue = pairing, flashing red = thermal fault, pulsing amber = low battery.

### Software & Licensing
- Unite must be 22.1+ for TRIOS 5/6 recognition. If scanners are absent, remove residual USB drivers (`Device Manager → View hidden devices → Universal Serial Bus devices`) and reinstall Unite.
- License expiration warnings after RMA shipments occur when the faulty device is not checked in within 32 days. Confirm the RMA case in 3Shape eSupport shows "device received" before closing the ticket.
- When switching scanners between clinics, always de-register the device in Unite → Accounts; otherwise, calibration data remains locked to the previous site and prevents new logins.

### Escalation Triggers
- Collect logs via `C:\ProgramData\3Shape\Logs\TRIOS` and include the `*.tdslog` file.
- Record firmware, pod serial, tip serial, battery cycles, and Unite version.
- Provide photos of error messages and the physical condition of tips, calibration targets, and charging docks.
- Escalate immediately if the scanner emits burning odor, shows recurring Error 4110 (laser fault), or fails LED self-test on boot.
